dialog.title: Generate an email with AI
dialog.promptPlaceholder: e.g. A friendly welcome email for new users with a CTA button to confirm their account
dialog.promptPlaceholderRefine: e.g. Make the CTA button orange, shorten the intro paragraph, and add a footer with links to our social networks.

suggestions.label: Welcome email
suggestions.prompt: A warm welcome email for new users of a modern SaaS product. Open with a short, friendly greeting, explain the one thing to do first, and finish with a single prominent CTA button to get started. Keep it under 150 words with generous spacing.

suggestions.label: Product launch
suggestions.prompt: A product launch announcement email. Start with a bold hero section (headline + supporting line + hero image placeholder), then three short feature highlights with icons or small images, and end with a strong CTA button to try the product. Confident, energetic tone.

suggestions.label: Monthly newsletter
suggestions.prompt: A clean monthly newsletter with a short intro from the team, three article teasers (title, one-sentence summary, Read more link each), and a footer with social links and an unsubscribe line. Editorial, calm tone with clear separation between stories.

suggestions.label: Abandoned cart
suggestions.prompt: An abandoned-cart reminder email. Gently remind the reader they left items behind, show a product image placeholder with name and price, add one line of reassurance (free returns or support), and a single CTA button to complete the purchase. Helpful, no-pressure tone.

suggestions.label: Event invite
suggestions.prompt: An event invitation email for a live online webinar. Lead with the event name and a one-line value promise, list date, time, and duration in a scannable block, introduce the speaker in one sentence, and close with an RSVP CTA button plus an add-to-calendar link.

suggestions.label: Verification code
suggestions.prompt: A minimal one-time verification code email. A short line explaining the code was requested, the 6-digit code displayed large and centered, a note that it expires in 10 minutes, and a quiet line telling the reader to ignore the email if they didn't request it. No images, no marketing.

suggestionsRefine.label: Change CTA color
suggestionsRefine.prompt: Change the primary CTA button to a warm orange background color with white text. Keep the button text, link, spacing, and overall layout exactly as they are. Adjust any complementary accents so the new orange reads well on the current background.

suggestionsRefine.label: Add a footer
suggestionsRefine.prompt: Add a footer section at the bottom of the email. Include a one-line tagline about the company, a row of small social media icons linking to Twitter, LinkedIn and Instagram, and a muted unsubscribe text link. Use a subtle divider above the footer to separate it from the main content. Do not touch any existing blocks.

suggestionsRefine.label: More formal tone
suggestionsRefine.prompt: Rewrite the body copy in a more formal, professional tone, suitable for a B2B audience. Keep the structure, CTAs, images, and technical details intact — only update wording. Avoid casual expressions, slang, or exclamation marks.

suggestionsRefine.label: Shorten the copy
suggestionsRefine.prompt: Tighten the body copy so the email reads at a glance. Combine or remove redundant paragraphs, keep every heading and CTA, and preserve critical information (dates, amounts, codes, links) verbatim. Target about half of the current text length.

suggestionsRefine.label: Add a hero image
suggestionsRefine.prompt: Insert a hero image block at the very top of the email, above every other block. Use a placeholder URL, set the image to full-width, and align the existing heading and intro paragraph below it with comfortable padding. Do not remove or reorder any other blocks.

suggestionsRefine.label: Dark mode palette
suggestionsRefine.prompt: Switch the color palette to a dark mode look: dark backdrop, near-black canvas, light neutral text, and a vibrant accent color for CTAs and links. Keep all copy, CTAs, layout, and spacing identical — only the colors change.
